implementation_notes: The typed realization is generated stubs: a .proto compiled with @grpc/proto-loader (or ts-proto) yields a client whose typed unary call marshals and ships the request over a long-lived channel, and a service implementation object whose method runs after unmarshalling on the other side - the forwarder and receiver exist as generated code, and the compiler enforces the message contract the classic pattern leaves to discipline. Where the peer cannot speak gRPC, TypeScript does what JavaScript does (node:net plus a length-prefixed codec) but keeps the wire shape in types: a discriminated-union Message, a codec pair and an exhaustive switch for dispatch. Keep the hand-rolled form when the framing must match an existing protocol; prefer the generated client for new peer-to-peer services.
pitfalls: Generated clients are meant to be reused: one per call leaks channels and subchannels until the process runs out of ports.
A handler that throws instead of calling callback(err) leaves the call hanging until deadline; mixups between callback and promise-style APIs double-call.
Types that mirror the .proto but silently drop unknown fields mask version skew - keep an explicit version in the message and validate before dispatch.
